title: Credential adapter: graceful streaming reconnect + multi-token rotation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers using long-lived API keys and enterprise SSO tokens face disrupted streaming sessions when credentials rotate or expire. Current SDKs either drop streams on 401/403 or retry blindly, causing duplicated outputs, user-visible errors, or stalled streams. We need a standardized credential adapter pattern across Python/TS/Go SDKs that: 1) supports multiple credential sources (API key, short-lived SSO token via refresh, external credential provider), 2) proactively refreshes tokens with a configurable grace window, 3) enables seamless streaming reconnect with resume tokens/KV cache preservation, and 4) documents secret handling guidance for local dev and CI so customers follow best practices.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a pluggable credential provider interface usable from Python/TS/Go
Provider interface supports synchronous attach and an async/subscribe refresh hook for short-lived tokens
Streaming client automatically attempts auth-refresh + resume flow on 401/403 without user-visible duplication for idempotent endpoints
Default SDK implementation uses env var -> file -> metadata server provider chain and documents how to inject enterprise SSO refreshers
Security doc added: no tokens in logs, masked telemetry, guidance for local dev secret stores (direnv/secret-store), and CI secret patterns
E2E tests cover rotation during active streaming and assert exactly-once semantics for idempotent messages or best-effort deduplication guidance for non-idempotent workloads
implementation_plan: Design a minimal credential provider interface for each language (sync attach(token header), async preflight/refresh, optional on-demand refresh callback)
Implement default chain provider (ENV -> credentials file with TTL metadata -> GCE/AWS metadata server)
Implement an Enterprise SSO refresher sample that exchanges a short-lived assertion for service tokens and caches them with expiry metadata
Add streaming reconnect orchestration: on auth failure, pause consumer, call provider.refresh(), re-establish stream with resume token and replay pending client buffer if necessary
Add proactive refresh: token refreshed when time_to_expiry < grace_window (default 60s) with randomized jitter
Wire telemetry events (auth.refresh_attempt, auth.refresh_success, auth.refresh_failure) with token hash only (no plaintext)
Write E2E test harness that simulates token rotation mid-stream and verifies resume behavior
Update SDK docs and create migration guide and quickstart snippets
compatibility_matrix: The credential adapter API is backward-compatible for basic API key usage: existing env var and header-based usage continues to work. New proactive refresh and provider chain are opt-in via client config. Streaming resume flow requires server support for resume tokens; fallback is unary reconnect.
migration_notes: For customers using long-lived API keys: no immediate change required. Recommend rotating keys and moving to short-lived tokens + refresh flow for higher security.
For enterprise SSO: provide an example refresh lambda that exchanges SSO assertion for service token; place it behind customer-managed KMS and standardize the refresh endpoint URL in SDK config.

CLI/local-dev: document use of .redwood/credentials.json with file locking and TTL metadata to avoid accidental check-ins. Recommend direnv or pass for local stash. CI: use secrets manager integrations and inject token via environment variables at runtime only.
rollout_plan: Feature branch with adapters and sample implementations merged behind feature flag 'credential_adapter_v2'
Canary release to SDK beta users and internal platform teams for 2 weeks
Gradual enable by default after 3 successful canary customers and key metrics within thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for provider chain evaluation order and TTL parsing
Integration: simulate metadata server rotation events and assert refresh() is called and new token used
Streaming E2E: start a stream, force token expiry mid-stream, ensure resume token used and no duplicate payloads for idempotent operations
Chaos test: intermittent metadata server + network partitions; ensure backoff and no token leakage to logs
Security tests: verify tokens are never emitted in logs or telemetry; token hashes only
docs_todo: Add 'Credential provider' conceptual doc with diagrams showing provider chain and refresh lifecycle
Add language-specific migration guides (Python, TypeScript, Go) with code samples
Write troubleshooting guide for common 401/403 streaming issues
Short checklist for security reviewers and SOC teams
security_considerations: Do not log token strings anywhere; only log stable token identifiers or hashes using a cryptographic digest
When caching on disk, restrict file permissions (600) and store only encrypted blobs when possible
Recommend customers use short-lived tokens with narrow scopes and rotate keys regularly
Provide clear guidance for handling refresh failures: fail closed for high-sensitivity tenants, fail open with rate-limited fallback for low-sensitivity
Audit event requirements: emit auth.refresh_attempt and auth.refresh_result with user_id, tenant_id, provider_type, and token_hash
